To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present an optimal solution for offline traffic regulation under the constraint of the budget and the ISP tolerance of bandwidth spiking, and an online traffic scheduling algorithm to achieve a near-optimal solution.
we have presented a novel approach to regulate the traffic volume in a network under the constraint of the budget and the percentile-based pricing scheme.

(a) the offline problem is a convex optimization problem and can be solved in polynomial time; (b) the online problem is a dynamic optimization problem and can also be solved in polynomial per period time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how to allocate a given amount of budget to regulate the traffic volume such that the bandwidth spiking can be controlled within a predetermined range.
the problem of how to regulate the traffic volume in a way that the ISP is satisfied and the customer is happy.
how to make the traffic regulation more effective under the constraint of the predetermined budget.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, under the percentile-based policy, the customer can effectively regulate the traffic volume by adjusting the scheduling policy.
the traffic regulation problem is a challenging one, and the solutions proposed here are useful for the ISP to regulate the traffic volume of its customers.
the proposed traffic regulation scheme can achieve the goal of reducing the bandwidth spikes to a level that the ISP can handle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed traffic scheduling algorithm is able to reduce the traffic volume while keeping the traffic spiking under control.
the proposed solutions can effectively reduce the amount of bandwidth spicing while maintaining a high utilization of bandwidth.
, with our solutions, a customer can achieve a good trade-off between the traffic volume and the amount of bandwidth spicking.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, under the percentile-based billing policy, the customer should regulate the traffic volume to avoid the peak bandwidth usage as much as possible, while the ISP can tolerate a small amount of band-width spike.
the customer can effectively control the traffic volume and the traffic regulation is not sensitive to the traffic demand pattern.
the optimal solution for the online case is very close to the one for the offline case.
